provenance.no-item-state-classes: CONFIRMED ABSENCE, checked directly against the literal className string of `RadioGroupItem`: there is NO `data-[state=checked]:` class of any kind — `aspect-square size-4 shrink-0 rounded-full border border-input text-primary shadow-xs transition-[color,box-shadow] outline-none focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring/50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50 aria-invalid:border-destructive aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20 dark:bg-input/30 dark:aria-invalid:ring-destructive/40` contains disabled/focus-visible/aria-invalid variants but NOTHING keyed on data-state — a real, sourced finding: the ITEM container is completely interaction-invariant with respect to checked/unchecked, unlike checkbox's own item (which fills solid via `data-[state=checked]:bg-primary`). The whole checked signal is the Indicator's presence.
provenance.no-hover-no-pressed: CONFIRMED ABSENCE, checked directly against BOTH className strings (Root and Item): no `hover:`, no `active:` class of any kind anywhere.
provenance.root-gap: RadioGroup's own className: `grid gap-3` = 12px, a real, sourced layout gap — unlike checkbox and switch, which own NO label/layout gap of their own since they render a single control rather than a group of them.
provenance.no-group-disabled-confirmed: The canonical `radio-group.tsx` file itself does not explicitly forward a `disabled` prop anywhere in its own literal source (Root simply spreads `...props`); Radix's own published API for RadioGroup.Root DOES document a group-level `disabled` per the linked docs, so this is recorded [R] rather than [S] — the capability plausibly exists via prop-spreading + Radix's own context, but is not confirmed by a grep of THIS clone's literal code the way item-level `disabled` (confirmed directly in radio-group-disabled.tsx) is.
